assumptions: A1. Synthetic credentials may sign in to demonstrate revocable sessions; no particular account list, password policy beyond a usable new password, or signed-in content is specified.

A2. Consistently normalized email identifies a synthetic account. Only the static sign-in composition is observed; reset, error, success and authenticated screens and their copy are proposed, not pictured.
A3. Authorized local tests or same-process demonstration code inspect reset links and successful-reset events in a private in-memory sink; no real email or public link inspection endpoint exists.
A4. Interpret five reset requests per account per hour as a rolling 3600-second window of accepted requests for each known synthetic account; do not infer a numeric quota for unknown identifiers.
A5. Interpret expiry as usable while now is strictly earlier than issued_at plus 30 minutes and invalid at or after that instant; this boundary convention is a design interpretation.

A6. One process and one isolated in-memory store are the local demonstration boundary. A restart loses accounts' mutable state, sessions, quotas, tokens and notifications; neither persistence nor multi-worker coordination is promised.

architecture_summary: Prospective local-only Python 3.12 Flask application factory renders Jinja sign-in and recovery pages and injects a UTC clock, cryptographic token generator, locked process-local synthetic-account/session/reset store and private in-memory notification sink. A revocable server-side session registry plus account epoch guards each protected request. Recovery accepts at most five known-account requests in a rolling hour while returning the same public acknowledgement for equivalent known, unknown and suppressed submissions; eligible links use random bearer tokens, a digest-only reset index and private sink delivery. An unused token remains usable only before 30 minutes from issuance. Reset POST revalidates and atomically commits a password-hash change, one-time token consumption, revocation of all account sessions and one owner-addressed sink event. Server-rendered sign-in styling follows only the observed static image; unpictured screens are proposals. Pytest will verify routes, private effects, boundaries and multiple clients; local documentation will state process-loss, single-worker, no-email and no-deployment limitations. This is a design, not a claim that the application or tests exist.

hosting.notes: Local execution only. Do not provision hosting, deploy, or add deployment workflows or instructions.

tasks.title: Local Flask foundation
tasks.description: Create the Python 3.12 Flask application factory, Jinja template/static-asset foundation, injectable UTC clock, isolated process-local memory store and synthetic hashed-account seed/fixtures. Do not connect a real identity store or production service.
acceptance_criteria: A documented local Python 3.12 invocation starts Flask and serves a server-rendered HTML page.
Two independently constructed app instances do not share synthetic accounts or mutable runtime state.
Inspection finds no real-account integration; this task establishes injectable state/time, not a deployed application.

tasks.title: Sign-in screen and revocable sessions
tasks.description: Render the pictured sign-in card and exact visible labels/placeholders/footer using semantic HTML and a local stylesheet. Implement password type=password (actual masking is an implementation requirement, not image-observed behavior), visible focus and associated labels; verify synthetic password hashes; protect POSTs with CSRF; create opaque registry-backed sessions with an account epoch and guarded /account; provide CSRF-protected sign-out. No unpictured signed-in-page appearance is asserted.
acceptance_criteria: GET /sign-in returns the outlined card on white, bold heading, labeled email with name@example.com, labeled password with ******** and type=password, blue underlined recovery link, wide dark button and exact footer.
Valid synthetic credentials reach an authenticated /account across requests; invalid credentials and CSRF failures do not.
A removed session or mismatched epoch fails the next protected request; a signed cookie alone does not grant access.

tasks.title: Private recovery request and quota
tasks.description: Make the pictured recovery link navigate to a proposed server-rendered labeled email request form. For a syntactically valid known synthetic account, enforce a locked rolling five-accepted-requests/3600-second window, generate a cryptographically random URL-safe reset token, index only its digest and issued-at time, and record the link in a private in-memory sink. Unknown identifiers and suppressed known-account requests issue no links, but use the same public acknowledgement as accepted requests. Never display a private link or expose the sink over HTTP.
acceptance_criteria: The link opens GET /forgot-password and valid request submissions return a rendered acknowledgement.
Otherwise equivalent known, unknown and suppressed POSTs have identical public status, headers and body without identifier, quota or link; comparison uses equivalent CSRF/session context.
Five known-account requests inside the rolling hour produce five private links, the sixth produces none, and a request at the oldest acceptance's +3600-second boundary can produce a new one.
Unknown identifiers create no link; no external delivery occurs.

tasks.title: Single-use reset and atomic completion
tasks.description: Render a proposed labeled new-password form for a valid link and a neutral unavailable-link state otherwise. On POST, validate CSRF/input and recheck digest, consumption and issue-based expiry under the same lock used by session creation; complete the new password hash, consumed token, account epoch/session revocation and one private owner-addressed success event together, before returning success. Keep link/password out of public responses and logs; no external notification service.
acceptance_criteria: An unused link at 29:59 since issuance accepts a new password; a separate unused link at 30:00 or later cannot update it.
A link permits one successful completion only, including against simultaneous/replayed submissions; failed submissions add no success event.
The old password ceases to sign in and the new one works after success.
Two or more previously authenticated, independent clients all fail the next protected request.
Each completed reset records exactly one owner-addressed in-memory notification, never a notification claiming external delivery.

tasks.title: Pytest regression suite
tasks.description: Add independent pytest fixtures for app factory, fixed/advancing UTC clock, synthetic accounts, private sink and multiple client cookie jars. Implement TC-001 through TC-022 in the Markdown verification matrix as automated checks; use no sleeps, live account or network notification. Run the suite locally with python3.12 -m pytest after implementing the application. This is a separate test task: TASK-001 through TASK-004 implement behavior and REQ-022 requires runnable pytest coverage here.
acceptance_criteria: python3.12 -m pytest is documented and runs the tests for the sign-in/reset behavior under Python 3.12.
Tests assert both public outcomes and private effects, including five/six/boundary, before/at-expiry, replay, independent-client session invalidation and owner event per success.
TC-001–TC-022 collectively exercise every REQ-001–REQ-022 without pretending to test visual browser behavior from an image alone; no test is reported as passed in this design.

tasks.title: Local documentation and delivery audit
tasks.description: Document local Python 3.12 setup, Flask startup, python3.12 -m pytest, synthetic credentials and authorized same-process/private-test sink inspection. Document process-restart state loss, single-worker limits, non-durable quota/revocation, no real account or notification delivery, and missing production-grade reliability/security operations. Review the delivered repository for the explicit no-deployment constraint; do not add deployment code, workflows, instructions or perform deployment.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can follow local-only setup/testing and identify why the demo is not production-ready.
Inspection confirms accounts are synthetic, sink remains memory-only, and tests have a runnable command.

Delivery/repository inspection finds no newly added deployment workflows or deploy instructions and no deployment action is performed; REQ-023 and REQ-024 are verified by documentation/repository inspection, not claimed to require pytest.
